items.title: Bobby Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: I think Louis Armstrong really showed the whole world... along with his contemporaries, Johnny Dodds and Kid Ory and the other ones that were on the records with him.

ctx.x: Great. You’ve mentioned the “Hot Five” and “Hot Seven” a couple of times. What was it about those particular recordings that really were such milestones, in your eyes?

In the first place they were called “race records” I guess they were called. They all sold a million records. Each copy that came out on 78s. And Louis Armstrong was just a genius of a cornet player on those records. That was just a recording band. They never played out in a club or anything like that. All they did was get together to record. And I think Louis Armstrong really showed the whole world, including today, everybody that’s playing trumpet, Louis Armstrong had an influence on everybody, and especially…
The sound of the instruments that come off those old 78s is interesting. The technology of the time kind of flavored what everything sounded like.
